rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a good-quality blastocyst and appropriately notes single-image limitations, but it overstates confidence in visible ICM/TE detail and describes features like a coherent peripheral TE rim and upper-left ICM that are not clearly discernible in this image.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, tubal factor, semen parameters, BMI, endometrium, and first-cycle status with embryo quality and prognosis.
Reasoning is logical and internally consistent, with appropriate caveats about morphology versus ploidy; only minor issue is somewhat broad confidence from a limited image.

Recommendations are largely evidence-based and consistent with standard IVF practice, including SET in a young patient and caution about hydrosalpinx; minor overreach includes discussing PGT-A and add-ons without stronger indication.

Provides practical next steps for transfer management and contingency planning, including SET, hydrosalpinx review, luteal support, and lifestyle advice, though some recommendations remain somewhat general.
